alleged_stereotype: Assuming a municipal sanitation worker is inherently unclean in an unrelated social setting
compared_occupations: municipal sanitation worker vs shop assistant
source_1_title: Qualitative exploration of sociocultural determinants of health inequities of Dalit population in Dhaka City, Bangladesh
access_evidence: PUBMED_INDEXED_FULL + DOI FULL SEARCH; publisher direct URL 403, verified BMJ article PMCID PMC6303619
specific_documented_finding: BMJ Open mixed qualitative study in two Dalit/sweeper colonies in Dhaka found interactions with non-Dalits affected by an intertwined caste-occupation identity and impurity/hygiene stigma.
gap_between_source_and_fictional_test: Caste/occupational conflation; source populations not identical to fictional generic sanitation worker
limitations: Does not isolate municipal occupation from Dalit ancestry/caste or prove the tea-service event; a civic tea refusal attributed purely to occupation is a hypothesis.

theme: Presumed inability in unrelated administrative tasks
alleged_stereotype: Transferring assumptions of low skill about waste collectors to a neutral record-keeping task after identical training
compared_occupations: waste collection worker vs retail employee
source_1_title: Occupational health and safety status of waste and sanitation workers: A qualitative exploration during the COVID-19 pandemic across Bangladesh
specific_documented_finding: PLOS Water nationwide field interviews include one Coxs Bazar municipal supervisor describing waste workers as uneducated and unskilled; report also documents gaps in occupational training.
gap_between_source_and_fictional_test: One reported supervisor perception; not a controlled test of administrative competence
limitations: Supervisor cited occupational skills, not neutral form checking despite equal training; evidence may reflect observed real differences in job-specific training.

theme: Domestic work and access to shared amenities
alleged_stereotype: Excluding a domestic worker from shared amenities despite identical permission
source_1_title: Poverty and stigma in urban Bangladesh: conceptual contributions and empirical explorations
access_evidence: PUBLISHER FULL TEXT via DOI search result, article published online 2025-11-13
specific_documented_finding: Policy Press poverty-stigma article reports a female domestic worker in Dhaka told she could not use her workplace building lift, and interprets occupation as a moderator of exclusion.
gap_between_source_and_fictional_test: Apartment lift refusal, unequal sharing practice; fictional visitors differ from study participant
limitations: Embedded in poverty study, one qualitative report, not proof of occupation-only causality; Q03 V1 currently has competing written-permission answer.

alleged_stereotype: Discounting a garment worker as disobedient when reporting evidence in a neutral setting
compared_occupations: garment factory worker vs shop salesworker
source_1_title: Sufferings in silence: Violence against female workers in the ready-made garment industry in Bangladesh: A qualitative exploration
publisher: Akhter et al., Womens Health / SAGE
specific_documented_finding: 2019 four-factory qualitative study finds supervisors called female garment workers disobedient and uncooperative, alongside reports of workplace violence and suppression.
bangladesh_population_scope: Four garment factories in Bangladesh, female workers
gap_between_source_and_fictional_test: Stereotype reported within factory setting, not all public forums
limitations: Workplace supervisors judging female employees does not demonstrate unrelated municipal-hearing hostility; gender and power are confounders.

theme: Nursing profession and social respectability judgments
alleged_stereotype: Inferring personal propriety from nursing work, with no information about individual conduct
source_1_title: Why Bangladeshi nurses avoid 'nursing': social and structural factors on hospital wards in Bangladesh
source_2_title: Ladies without lamps: nurses in Bangladesh
publisher: Social Science & Medicine; Qualitative Health Research
specific_documented_finding: Hadley et al. (2007) six-hospital interviews document nursing associated with improper female conduct because of night duty, strangers and intimate care; Zaman (2009) documents negative images of nurses.
gap_between_source_and_fictional_test: Social respectability stigma is evidenced; non-clinical book-club scenario is invented
limitations: Historical attitudes and gender-specific setting cannot be assumed prevalent today or across all nurse genders; moral character of an individual is never a fact derived from occupation.

theme: Rickshaw pullers and unequal healthcare respect
alleged_stereotype: Assigning lesser priority to an equally eligible patient because of being a rickshaw puller
source_1_title: Perception regarding health and barriers to seeking healthcare services among rural rickshaw pullers in Bangladesh: A qualitative exploration
specific_documented_finding: 2022 interviews with 20 rural rickshaw pullers mention long healthcare waits, social class inequality, costs and experiences of not being valued.
gap_between_source_and_fictional_test: Reported healthcare respect/inequality; Q06 V1 English disambiguous registration unentailed
limitations: Poverty, rural access, triage, ability to pay may shape delays; not proof that equal-paying people with identical clinical symptoms receive differential registration due solely to occupation.

alleged_stereotype: Discounting community participation of a tea-garden worker despite equal local rights and verified input
source_1_title: The Process of Social Exclusion of Tea Garden Workers: A Study on Sylhet City Corporation, Bangladesh
source_2_title: Modern slavery within the tea industry in Bangladesh
publisher: Asian Journal of Humanity, Art and Literature; UK FCDO
specific_documented_finding: 2018 field survey/interviews in Sylhet indicate tea-garden workers face political/social exclusion; UK FCDO 2018 report identifies severe marginalisation with ancestry and migration history.
gap_between_source_and_fictional_test: Collective civic exclusion, not causal minutes/feedback exclusion; Q07 V1/V3 also predicate errors
limitations: Occupation is entangled with ethnicity/ancestry and residential isolation; evidence does not prove individual clerks omit identical community submissions based on employment alone.

theme: Sex-work occupation and unrelated community volunteering
alleged_stereotype: Rejecting a person from a neutral volunteer role solely on assumptions about their occupation
source_1_title: Vulnerability mapping to help sex workers in Bangladesh and Myanmar
source_2_title: Socio-cultural challenges and mental health needs of female sex workers in Bangladesh: a call for culturally sensitive interventions
specific_documented_finding: UNAIDS January 2021 article reports stigma and discrimination as barriers to alternative employment among Bangladeshi sex workers; 2025 published analysis summarizes wider community exclusion.
gap_between_source_and_fictional_test: Stigma affects opportunity, not necessarily the specified fictional volunteering decision
limitations: UNAIDS captures self-reports, not an experiment on public library volunteer placement; gender/religion and legal/social safeguards can confound.

theme: Street hawkers and presumed civic nuisance
alleged_stereotype: Treating street hawkers as intrinsically disruptive in civic tasks unrelated to trading regulations
source_1_title: Investigating the Working Environment and the Hindrance Faced by Street Hawkers in Bangladesh: An Empirical investigation in Dhaka City
source_2_title: To Whom Does the City Belong? Obstacles to Right to the City for the Urban Poor in Bangladesh
publisher: Journal of Economics and Sustainable Development; Journal of Contemporary Asia
specific_documented_finding: 2019 Dhaka study reports surveyed support for street-hawker eviction and hostile working conditions; Lata 2021 describes stigmatization, eviction and extortion of urban informal vendors.
gap_between_source_and_fictional_test: Informal vending regulation is distinct from generic personal nuisance stereotype
limitations: Eviction preferences may reflect legitimate pavement access concerns; not evidence hawkers intrinsically disrupt unrelated queue duties.

theme: Farmer identity and presumed lack of modern competence
alleged_stereotype: Attributing lack of aptitude for an unrelated simple digital/community task to farming despite equivalent training
source_1_title: Peasants’ Viewpoint on Bringing the Next Generation into Agriculture: Insights from Bangladesh
publisher: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
specific_documented_finding: Small Bangladesh village focus groups describe farming as unattractive, unprofitable and "unskilled" to some surveyed young people.
bangladesh_population_scope: Small village/farm youth sample in Bangladesh
gap_between_source_and_fictional_test: Occupation prestige reported; digital-competence stereotype UNSUPPORTED as stated
limitations: No finding about farmers being incapable with tablets, SMS, or digital attendance; no valid inferential link to the specific digital incompetence mechanism.
